title: Kalimpong, Lava and the villages by shared jeep
meta_description: Shared jeep routes, fares and timings for Siliguri, Kalimpong, Lava, Lolegaon, Pedong, Darjeeling and Gangtok, and when a reserved car is worth it.
summary: Shared jeeps link Siliguri, Kalimpong, Lava, Lolegaon, Pedong, Darjeeling and Gangtok for a fraction of a reserved car, often ₹60–300 a seat, indicative 2026. They leave when full, mostly in the morning. Use them for the long legs and hire a car only for the villages beyond Lava that have no service.

sections.heading: How shared jeeps work here
paras: In the Kalimpong hills the shared jeep, usually a Mahindra Bolero, Tata Sumo or similar, is the bus. Local people ride it to school, to market and to hospital, and visitors can too. Each jeep takes about ten passengers: two beside the driver, then two rows behind. Luggage goes on the roof under a tarpaulin. You buy a seat at a counter or from the driver, and the jeep leaves when every seat is sold.

That last point shapes your day. Jeeps run most often in the morning, when people head to town and back, and thin out by early afternoon. On a quiet route the last one may leave at 1 or 2 pm. If you arrive at 4 pm, you can still go, but you will be offered the whole jeep at a reserved price. Plan transfer days to start early.

Fares are fixed by the local drivers' associations and are posted at bigger stands, so bargaining is not usual. They change with fuel prices and diversions. All fares in this guide are indicative for 2026; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Routes, fares and times
paras: These are the routes most visitors use. Times are for normal road conditions; add one to three hours when NH10 along the Teesta is closed and traffic takes the detours by Gorubathan or Peshok.

sections.heading: From Siliguri, NJP and Bagdogra
paras: Kalimpong jeeps leave Siliguri from the stands near the Tenzing Norgay bus terminus on Hill Cart Road and from the Panitanki More area. NBSTC, the state bus company, also runs buses from the terminus to Kalimpong for a little less than a jeep seat, slower and at fixed times. From NJP station, a shared auto or a short taxi ride brings you to the jeep stands. From Bagdogra airport, an app cab or prepaid taxi to Siliguri town costs a few hundred rupees and still leaves a couple well ahead of a ₹3,000–4,500 reserved car to Kalimpong.

The ride follows the Teesta past Sevoke and the Coronation Bridge, then up the river to Teesta Bazaar and the final climb to Kalimpong. Sit on the left going up for river views. If you get car sick, ask for a middle-row seat and eat lightly. For the return, buy your seat at the Kalimpong motor stand the evening before, and leave at least three hours of margin before a train from NJP or a flight from Bagdogra.

sections.heading: Beyond Kalimpong: Lava, Lolegaon and Pedong
paras: Jeeps to Lava, Lolegaon, Pedong and Algarah leave from Kalimpong's motor stand in the town centre. Ask at the counter the evening before for the first departure, and arrive 20 minutes early to get a seat. The Lava road climbs through Algarah into pine and fir; the jeep drops you in the small bazaar, a short walk from the forest lodge and the Neora Valley permit office.

Lolegaon has fewer jeeps, often two or three a day, so it is the route most likely to leave you waiting. Pedong is easy, with jeeps through the morning, and from Pedong a short local ride or a walk of a few kilometres reaches Sillery Gaon.

The real gaps are between villages. There is no regular service from Lava to Rishyap, Kolakham or Lolegaon on most days. You can walk the 4 km forest trail from Lava to Rishyap with a guide, or hire a local car. These short hires are where we spend money even on a budget trip.
list: Lava to Rishyap, reserved car: about ₹800–1,200, or walk the 4 km forest trail with a guide.
Lava to Kolakham, reserved car: about ₹800–1,500.
Lava to Lolegaon, reserved car: about ₹1,500–2,500.
Neora Valley from Lava: permitted park jeeps only, ₹1,500–2,500 per jeep, shared with other visitors if you ask at the forest office.

sections.heading: When a reserved car is the better deal
paras: Shared jeeps are cheapest per person, but not always cheapest per group. Four people pay for four seats, which on Siliguri to Kalimpong comes to ₹800–1,200, against ₹3,000–4,500 for the whole car. That is still a saving. But on village days, when you need four or five short legs, a car hired for the day at ₹3,000–4,500 is often cheaper than piecing together jeeps and local hires, and far less tiring.

Reserve a car when you travel with small children or seniors, when you carry big suitcases, when you arrive after 2 pm, and for days that start before dawn, such as a sunrise at Tiffin Dara or Jhandi Dara. Also reserve one when NH10 is closed, since shared jeeps on the detour routes are fewer and fill quickly with local passengers who need them more.

sections.heading: Shared jeep tips from the road
paras: A few habits make shared travel easier and keep you on good terms with drivers and fellow passengers.
list: Pack in one soft bag; hard suitcases are awkward on a roof rack and take extra seats if they ride inside.
Cover your bag against rain and dust, and keep valuables, medicines and a jacket with you, not on the roof.
The front seats sell first. Book the evening before if you want one, and expect the same fare.
Carry small notes; drivers rarely have change for ₹500 at dawn.
Tea stops happen at Teesta Bazaar or Algarah. Ask how long before you wander off.
If someone elderly or unwell boards, offer the front seat. It matters here.
Ask the driver about the road before you pay in the rains; he will know if a stretch is closed.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps to Kalimpong leave from in Siliguri
faqs.a: From the stands near the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road and from the Panitanki More area. Jeeps leave when full, from early morning until about mid-afternoon. A seat costs ₹200–300, indicative 2026, and the trip takes 2.5 to 3.5 hours. Ask locals for the current stand, as counters sometimes move.

faqs.q: Is there a bus from Siliguri to Kalimpong
faqs.a: Yes. NBSTC, the North Bengal State Transport Corporation, runs buses from the Siliguri bus terminus to Kalimpong at set times through the day. They cost a little less than a jeep seat and are slower, with more stops. Buses suit travellers with time and light luggage. Check current timings at the terminus, as schedules change.

faqs.q: How do I get from Kalimpong to Lava without a car
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from the Kalimpong motor stand. Several leave each morning, the seat costs ₹100–150, indicative 2026, and the ride takes about 1.5 hours through Algarah. Buy your ticket the evening before or arrive early. The jeep drops you in Lava bazaar, a short walk from the forest lodge and the Neora permit office.

faqs.q: Is there a shared jeep from Lava to Rishyap
faqs.a: Not regularly. Most days there is no scheduled service between Lava and Rishyap. You can walk the 4 km forest trail, best uphill with a local guide, or hire a car for about ₹800–1,200, indicative 2026. Some homestays arrange pickups from Lava if you book with them. Carry luggage light if you plan to walk.

faqs.q: Can I travel from Kalimpong to Gangtok by shared jeep
faqs.a: Yes. Shared jeeps to Gangtok leave Kalimpong in the morning for about ₹250–400 a seat, indicative 2026, and take three to three and a half hours via the Teesta and Rangpo. Carry photo ID for the Sikkim checkpost; foreign nationals need a Sikkim permit. Check current status before you travel, since NH10 closures affect this route too.

faqs.q: Are shared jeeps safe for women travelling alone
faqs.a: Generally yes. Shared jeeps carry families, schoolchildren and office workers, and women travel alone on them every day. Sit beside other women where you can, travel in daylight, and keep your phone charged. If something feels wrong, get off at the next town; another jeep will come. Drivers and fellow passengers tend to look out for visitors.

faqs.q: What happens to shared jeeps when NH10 is closed
faqs.a: Jeeps take the detours, either by Gorubathan and Lava or by Darjeeling and Peshok. Journeys take one to three hours longer, fares rise a little, and fewer jeeps run, so seats sell out early. Ask at the stand about the day's route before you buy. Check current status before you travel, especially from June to September.

faqs.q: Can I book a shared jeep seat in advance
faqs.a: On busy routes, yes, but usually only in person, the evening before, at the counter where the jeep leaves. Few shared jeeps can be booked online. Paying for a front seat ahead is common. If you arrive on a late train, a reserved car is more reliable than hoping for a seat.

faqs.q: How much luggage can I take on a shared jeep
faqs.a: One medium bag per person is normal, and it goes on the roof under a tarpaulin. Very large suitcases may be refused or charged as an extra seat. Keep a small daypack inside with valuables, medicines, water and a jacket. Pack your roof bag in a plastic liner, because rain and dust find their way in.
